entry.title: The Bordeaux Conjecture of Borodin and Raspaud
entry.literal_statement: For a graph $G$, let $d^{\bigtriangledown}$ denote the minimum distance between distinct triangles of $G$. **Borodin and Raspaud's Bordeaux conjecture.** Every planar graph with $d^{\bigtriangledown}\geq 1$ and without $5$-cycles is $3$-colorable. This conjecture is presented as a planar graph 3-coloring problem related to the conjectures of Havel and Steinberg; the source does not provide evidence of resolution.
entry.assessment: Planarity, triangle distance and exclusion of5-cycles all essential. Steinberg counterexamples do not automatically satisfy this stronger triangle condition. No exact graph witness.

entry.title: Ma–Ma–Yeh conjecture on partial gamma-positivity of generalized Stirling permutation polynomials
entry.statement_literal:
Let $n\geq 1$ and $0\leq i\leq n$. Write

$$
\Jsp_{n,i}(x,y,z):=\sum_{\pi\in\mathcal{JSP}_{n,i}}x^{\operatorname{asc}(\pi)}y^{\operatorname{des}(\pi)}z^{\operatorname{plat}(\pi)}
$$

for the trivariate extension of $A_{n,i}(y)$. A trivariate polynomial $p(x,y,z)=\sum_i s_i(x,y)z^i$ is **partial $\gamma$-positive** when every coefficient $s_i(x,y)$ is homogeneous $\gamma$-positive, meaning that it is homogeneous and can be written as

$$
s_i(x,y)=\sum_k\gamma_k(xy)^k(x+y)^{d-2k}
$$

with all $\gamma_k\geq 0$. **Ma–Ma–Yeh conjecture.** For every $n\geq 1$ and $0\leq i\leq n$, the polynomial $\Jsp_{n,i}(x,y,z)$ is partial $\gamma$-positive. The conjecture concerns the coefficientwise gamma-positivity of the ascent–descent–plateau enumerators for generalized Stirling permutations; its status is not resolved in the supplied source context.
entry.disposition: Ma-Ma-Yeh partial gamma-positivity conjecture for Jacobi-Stirling plateau/descent/ascent polynomials: the reserved source itself proves it ("Specialization ... confirms a recent partial gamma-positivity conjecture due to Ma, Yeh and the second named author").
